notes:
Scope: the shipped catkin workspace ros/catkin_ws/src has one ROS package, ue4_bridge, a ROS 1 node that republishes UE4 ZMQ frames as sensor_msgs/Image. The package binds the fixed color stream /rgb_camera_0 (bgr8) and the metric depth stream /rgb_camera_0depth_range_mm (mono16) through cap.sensing.image.v1's selector profile and returns bounded local PNG artifacts. The topic names are assembled at run time from the shipped rgb_camera_%d template (demos/bluerov/unreal_proxy/config.py:10); the resolved literals are evidenced by demos/px4_gazebo/image_view.launch:4,7 and demos/px4_gazebo/orb_slam_ros/ORB_SLAM2/src/ros_rgbd.cc:68-69. NOT COVERED: rgb_camera_0down (the clone has no resolved literal name for it), rgb_camera_0depth_rgb8 (the colorized depth visualization; the metric range_mm stream is bound instead), rgb_camera_0depth_cam_info (hardcoded 320x240 geometry that does not describe the received image), the ZMQ control channels, UE4 renderer configuration, drone physics/SITL/MAVLink and the Docker/tmux deployment. The ue4_bridge node exposes no ROS stop, pause, reset or stepping interface; the demo drone control is external MAVLink/MAVROS or ZMQ, which this RosDriver cannot express. The upstream UE4/SITL deployment is container-based (README.md:5,10) and was not run here. The fake is a synthetic ROS-free protocol stand-in, not a replay of captured ROS traffic. It returns 2x2 placeholder frames; the deployment's UE4 render-target size is configured outside the clone and the clone fixes no size. Its depth samples are placeholders. Fidelity is F0 with no renderer, physics or pacing. The local artifact store's default 2 MiB per-artifact bound is an operator setting; a full-resolution UE4 frame may need an explicit larger store bound. The package declares only the fake backend .fake:FakeDronesimlab; the raw bgr8/mono16 Image messages are converted by the production RosBridge/ros_images path, not by fake.py. A live run needs the operator's rosbridge endpoint plus a running ue4_bridge node fed by the UE4 proxy, which was not constructed or tested here. No numeric Limit is declared because the only input is the closed camera selector. The G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning is expected: no actuating capability declares a limit. No hardware run and no live ROS validation; evidence is contract_checked only. driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null and this package is model-authored. The gate command exited 0 on the fake backend.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked both image bindings, all 13 facts, the image and frame bounds, the R0 fake-only scope and the fake against ue4_bridge.py, the demo configs, image_view.launch, ros_rgbd.cc and the UE4 proxies at the pin; the topic names and encodings are right. Four facts said more than their lines (a 'so a ROS topic does not exist' inference on 43-49, 'does not copy the image shape, so this package does not use it' on 92-93, and 'lazily' on 44-45 and 46-49, whose check is on line 43), and the fake and a test gave the colour stream frame_id camera_rgb although the bridge publishes it without setting a header (53-55; camera_rgb is only the colourized depth image's frame, 64). The reviewer narrowed or widened those facts, made three wordings precise and added two fidelity gaps (the unset colour header; float16 centimetres scaled by 10 before the uint16 cast, 69-72) in driver.py, made the fake's colour frame_id empty (fake.py), changed the colour case to expect it (test_driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged. For the human reviewer: Simulation only: the bridge republishes UE4 renderer frames. ZMQ SUBSCRIBE matches prefixes, so it also republishes rgb_camera_0down, and in the BlueROV demo rgb_camera_0l and rgb_camera_0r, under their own names. There is no actuation; closing a subscription stops observation only, not the renderer.
